Title: Kisnt KN85 Wireless Mechanical Keyboard, 75% Layout, Bluetooth/2.4GHz/USB-C, Custom RGB Backlit, Hot-Swappable Linear Switch, Creamy Sound for Gaming/Typing (Retro Beige)
Description: 【75% Space‑saving Layout】The KN85 series is a compact 85‑key keyboard (13.68" × 5.51" × 1.77") that keeps all the essentials (F1–F12, arrows, shortcuts) without the number pad. It frees up 25% of desk space for better mouse movement. Designed for small desks, laptop setups, gamers and minimalists. For frequent number‑pad input, choose our full‑size KN104 with a complete dedicated numpad, or opt for our new KN98 model — compact 99‑key that retains the numpad while saving desktop real‑estate
Category: Video Games,PC,Accessories,Gaming Keyboards
Reviews:
[{"reviewer_name": "Jen Degenhardt", "review_title": "Genuinely the best budget keyboard out there", "review_text": "I can’t recommend the kisnt KN85 enough. The RGB is bright (although the software isn’t great), It’s a good weight for a plastic keyboard, the colors it comes in are attractive, and the price is amazing. The most important part (to me) is the switches. They are Bsun purple switches, a smooth, creamy linear switch that sounds amazing. I genuinely use these in my other boards. It is made of plastic, but the plastic is sturdy. It is bluetooth, 2.4 ghz, and wired. Overall, this keyboard is worth it. I love this keyboard, i’ve bought two of them!", "review_rating": ""}, {"reviewer_name": "Harrison Phillips", "review_title": "Best board for the price, BY FAR !!", "review_text": "Great board especially at this price point. This really raises the bar for entry level products and makes it much more accessible. This thing will impress most seasoned enthusiast. I could see this thing attaining a similar status to the Aula F75.
You get really good acoustics, great switches (lubed BSUN Purples), gasket mounting AND hotswap.
I've been typing on it for a few days and the sound tests you see online are very accurate, board sounds very creamy and poppy, which makes for a very satisfying typing experience.
The RGB on this board is really bright and has some cool preset animations.
Definitely NOT office friendly, I took this thing to the office one day and had to swap it for a normal keyboard because it is quite loud. I enjoy the sound but I don't think my coworkers did. lol
Unfortunately I did notice that the space bar seems to make a really loud thunk which doesn't match the sound of the rest of the board, but you can fix this pretty easily with a rubber O-Ring or some foam inside the space bar.", "review_rating": ""}, {"reviewer_name": "Keith S", "review_title": "Super impressive for the price.", "review_text": "I'm shocked at the quality of this keyboard for the price. The main case is plastic but a is very good quality plastic. Obviously, it's not going to be aluminum at this price. The quality of the keycaps is also excellent. They are the more premium PBT plastic rather than the cheaper ABS plastic and they feel great. It even has more features than my other higher end mechanical keyboard as this one not only has wired USB (obviously), but also 2.4 Ghz dongle (which secures nicely in a little cutout of the bottom of the keyboard and held in magnetically), and a whooping 3 Bluetooth channels so you can pair this keyboard with many different devices at the same time.
I love the layout as well. It's a little smaller than a TKL layout keyboard, but without any compromises. Typically, I don't like 75% or less because you lose too many useful keys or they have them in a weird place, but this keyboard's layout is perfectly done. You still have all of your Home, End, PgUp, PgDn, Insert, Delete, and Print Screen and Pause/Break keys. The only key missing is the Scroll Lock key which is never used anyway so this is perfect.
It has nice RGB that lights up under and around the keys. Also comes with some extra switches and even a decent keycap and switch puller tool. Even comes a thin, cheap, plastic dust cover which I appreciate.", "review_rating": ""}, {"reviewer_name": "Michael", "review_title": "It's pretty good!", "review_text": "Chances are, you've found this keyboard after reading a number of Reddit threads or watching a review or 2 on Youtube, and I can confirm they're all very correct to recommend this keyboard.
It's kind of obvious that it's not trying to be high-end, as evidenced by the all plastic build, basic and other creature-comforts that are left out, like volume knobs and little near-useless LED screens, but it is still a solid, well built keyboard with a decent-enough feature set.
But, it's a keyboard, so if we're being real, its the tactile feel of typing on this thing along with it's really nice, satisfying "creamy" sound (at least that's what I've heard it called, though I still don't quite get why) that makes you want mechanical keyboard like this and this one does the thing real well while also looking pretty dang nice at the same time (I got the gray gradient version with side-printed keycaps. The battery life using the included USB 2.4G wireless dongle is exceptionally good and it also has RGB backlighting with 20 preprogrammed lighting modes, if you're into that thing, but I've got it set to a static color and it looks good enough for me.", "review_rating": ""}, {"reviewer_name": "Angela", "review_title": "Amazing, and truly worth the price.", "review_text": "It's a truly amazing keyboard, it feels great, looks great, and sounds great. I have only one issue with it, it's loud, but that's only an issue at night. The ergonomics feel pretty good, and the switches are very nice and responsive. Everything feels high quality, especially for this price. Very worth it and affordable.
The backlight is a nice touch, it can be disabled and enabled, along with changing the color and speed.
Note:
"Mom if you're seeing this, I wrote this review" -your son.", "review_rating": ""}, {"reviewer_name": "Wiaan", "review_title": "Amazing keyboard for the price", "review_text": "This keyboard sounds even better than the reviews claim. Before buying, I came across a few comments suggesting that some of the internal padding had been removed or that the overall quality had declined as the keyboard became more popular. After using it myself, I can confidently say that those concerns were unfounded.
The build quality is excellent, the typing experience is incredibly satisfying, and the switches feel fantastic. Every keypress sounds and feels premium, making it a joy to use for both work and gaming.
So far, I’ve only tested the 2.4GHz wireless mode, so I can’t comment on the wired or Bluetooth performance. However, based on my experience, I have no hesitation recommending it.
For the price, this keyboard offers outstanding value. It was absolutely worth the wait, especially considering I ordered it from the US and had it shipped to South Africa.", "review_rating": ""}, {"reviewer_name": "William Urling", "review_title": "The best value for a budget keyboard, hands down.", "review_text": "This keyboard has been an absolute dream, and the price cannot be beat. It uses bsun switches (I'm honestly not sure which, I've done some digging but can't find them), of which I got the linear version. These switches are nice, there is no noticeable scratch, a crisp bottom out, and the stabilizers are actually silent with no rattle or ticking. There is a variety of foam included, but they leave a bit of room in the case which keeps the board from sounding muted. There are NO SCREWS, so modding this thing is a breeze (might need a small flathead tho) and you have a lot of options straight out of the box. It also comes with a hotswap board, so you can lube the switches (already lubed, but do what you want) or change them out entirely. There are also FLIPPY FEET (2 STAGE!!) so you can adjust your typing angle. I have heard people complain about the software that comes with the board, but it turns out it is fully compatible with the Signal RGB app. Now I can assign any pattern I want, even outside of the presets! The lighting is very prominent since the LEDs are south-facing. 3 of the lights do not work in the software, but they are on the edge of the board with the modifier keys so they are not noticeable.
My ONLY gripe is that the keycaps are not very durable. I have been using mine for a few months now and the tops of the WASD keys are starting to become shiny and smoother. These are likely not PBT, but they are a very thick ABS so the sound stays deeper and fuller. However, a PBT set from a name brand manufacturer costs more than this entire keyboard, so this is an incredibly minor complaint.", "review_rating": ""}, {"reviewer_name": "Billlydee", "review_title": "Comfortable, creamy sound, easy set up.", "review_text": "Set up was a breeze, simply plug in. It charges in a few hours.
This keyboard is really nice. I like the “creamy” sound other viewers have described. A VERY light touch is all you need to type. I won’t say it’s sensitive, it just requires a light touch of each key. That is something I need to get used to.
I have a laptop set up on a riser, and needed a keyboard that will fit in the small space beneath it. This was my choice after reviewing MANY keyboards. I also wanted a laptop with raised keys, a mechanical keyboard. I like the “old school” feel of it.
Weight: it’s heavy. I won’t be traveling with it, so that doesn’t matter to me. But I love the heaviness of it. Feels secure in its spot.
Ergonomics: there are two levels if you want to change the angle. Three is you count not using the little feet at the back. I also have a padded hand/wrist rest for extra comfort (NOT INCLUDED) but the keyboard itself is comfortable to use.
Color: I would have preferred black to match my desk accessories and laptop, or blue my favorite color. I went for the least expensive option as the color doesn’t change the effectiveness of the device.", "review_rating": ""}, {"reviewer_name": "Gabriel Velázquez", "review_title": "Buen sonido y calidad por el precio, pero software y patas mejorables", "review_text": "El teclado superó mis expectativas en lo esencial: sonido “thock” muy placentero, pulsaciones firmes y tres modos de conexión que funcionan sin problema. La construcción se siente sólida; el plástico es grueso y limpio al tacto, de mejor calidad que en otros modelos de su rango.
Puntos a favor:
Excelente sensación y respuesta lineal.
Sonido grave-cremoso desde fábrica, sin necesidad de mods.
Muy buen valor por el precio: se acerca a prestaciones “custom” de gamas más altas.
Puntos a mejorar:
El software de administración fue inútil en dos PC. La página es confusa, y aunque el teclado fue reconocido, no ofrecía opciones reales de configuración.
La parte trasera utiliza un plástico más sencillo, y las gomas antideslizantes están pegadas con cinta doble faz que comenzó a despegarse desde el primer día. Me preocupa que se pierdan o necesiten ser reemplazadas pronto.", "review_rating": ""}, {"reviewer_name": "Diwakar", "review_title": "Fantastic Keybaord", "review_text": "Excellent Product", "review_rating": ""}, {"reviewer_name": "Billy", "review_title": "BEST KEYBOARD I HAVE EVER USED. WORTH EVERY PENNY.", "review_text": "Honestly, I am absolutely blown away with the quality of this kisnt KN85, it's hands down the best keyboard I have ever owned. First of all, the sound quality of the key click is insane, this thing is so thocky with the bsun switches, PBT double shot key caps, gasket mounts and multiple layers of dampening foam/silicone, genuinely such a pleasure to type with. It is even hot-swappable if you want to change or upgrade your switches. The battery life is amazing, first use never charged out of the box lasted over a full week of heavy daily use.
I find it very hard to find any fault with this keyboard whatsoever. One note is that the LED's are south-facing, so shine-through backlit keycaps won't work, I like double-shot caps for the thock, so this doesn't bother me one bit. But seriously, I have never been so happy to be typing at my desk. It has changed my whole experience. I watch reviews of £200-£500 keyboards, and I still think this is better.
All I will say is get it fast, as prices are constantly rising due to demand.", "review_rating": ""}, {"reviewer_name": "Ontarioo", "review_title": "It's really solid", "review_text": "looks and feels amazing, setup was easy and battery is lasting along time which is great. but the sound of the keyboard is so creamy, it really does sound like a premium keyboard. I also love the beige color scheme its very clean yet retro and the letters are bolded and of course its not a lousy 60% so you can enjoy all the key functions without having to press FN all the time", "review_rating": ""}, {"reviewer_name": "KM", "review_title": "Better than expected", "review_text": "Awesome keyboard that punches above its weight. Stock switches are louder than I'd like, but hey it's a custom keyboard, so just swap them out easily for anything you like. For the price it's great keyboard. ONLY major issue is I like separate numpad controllers (I put these on the right of my mouse so it's quicker) but Kisnt only make these seperate numpads for the two other colour schemes that exist. The beige and green scheme is missing.", "review_rating": ""}]

Title: Razer BlackWidow V4 X Mechanical Gaming Keyboard, Yellow Switches, Black
Description: YELLOW MECHANICAL LINEAR SWITCHES: With zero distance between actuation and reset points at 1.2mm and only 45g of force required — enjoy instant, rapid-fire inputs that are just as quiet thanks to built-in sound dampeners
Category: Video Games,PC,Accessories,Gaming Keyboards
Reviews:
[{"reviewer_name": "Hurting", "review_title": "It's a good board", "review_text": "Ok, so after spending a couple weeks with this board I can tell you-
A couple of things I wasn't really aware of-
1) Just how much pressure I'm used to applying at rest on keys
2) How much I relied on outside esc and ctrl keys for orientation
These keys are very sensitive compared to the old BW I've used for years. I've been accidentally entering a lot of keystrokes at rest. They are very quiet and soft stroking compared to the green switches in the older Black Widow I've retired. So if you want clicks, feedback or resistance look elsewhere. Believe it or not my main hesitation for getting this board was the outside left row of programmable keys. I was afraid that it would be in the way and get confused with my escape and control keys, which yes has been very challenging to get used to, but it's no fault of the board itself knowing what I was getting. I pulled up all those caps on that row and replaced with wider pudding caps for brighter distinction. Programed those keys to mirror their neighbors, esc ,Ctrl etc so that when an erroneous keystroke is made it should at least still be the function I was looking for, albeit orientation may be off from wasd. So anyway I'm having to look down a lot more at the keyboard and retraining my mind to orient off the *F key", "review_rating": ""}, {"reviewer_name": "Scott C", "review_title": "Durable and well built. Survived a liquid disaster.", "review_text": "I have the green switch version.
Durable and Chroma lighting is excellent. Put O rings in the keys to dampen slightly. Key feeling and clicks are a matter of personal preference.
Spilled coffee on this one twice. I thought the keyboard was toast after the last disaster spill. Keys weren't functioning and the leds were out. I took it apart and rinsed it out the affected areas heavily with alcohol. Blew the liquid out with compressed air/compressor. Works fine now.
After taking it apart I could see how good the quality was. Keyboard backplate is actually solid metal.
2 screws under the top two rubber foot pads. Careful, the pads tear easily.
18+- screws under the keys. Remove the keys to find them all.", "review_rating": ""}, {"reviewer_name": "Matt T.", "review_title": "Best Keyboard I've Had", "review_text": "Zero complaints, satisfying sound, a lot of cool features. Very satisying feeling when typing, not loud or clunky at all. You can tell the quality of the build by the weigh it feels and it's weight. I love also the volume wheel, so cool!", "review_rating": ""}, {"reviewer_name": "Connor Nanney", "review_title": "Great Keyboard, would buy again", "review_text": "Had it for a bit over a week now and it's been great. I originally had the Razer blackwidow V1 with the green clicks switches and it was great the thing finally crapped out on me a few weeks ago. The thing lasted me forever, was super durable and felt very responsive. My biggest complaint was it was hard to clean. So I decided to go with the newest version and try the Yellow switches. I didn't like the softer yellow switches at first but have come to like them and this keyboard solved the cleaning issue. My biggest problem was actually the Macro keys on the left hand side. With my old keyboard I used the edge of they keyboard to orient my hand without looking when gaming, this makes it hard to do that because my fingers end up on the macro keys. I've started to retrain myself to position properly but it wasn't easy. Other than that this keyboard is fantastic.", "review_rating": ""}, {"reviewer_name": "James", "review_title": "Works great, looks great", "review_text": "Awesome keyboard!", "review_rating": ""}, {"reviewer_name": "Angel", "review_title": "Solid Keyboard", "review_text": "Fun RGB lighting, fully customizable colors within the Razer lighting program. Lighting program is easy to use with plenty of tutorials on installation. Can customize individual keys for different lighting when pressed. Extra macro buttons on the left will take some getting used to, but just imagine what all you can assign them as. Solid keyboard in terms of weight, back wings to lift up to have it at a slight angle. Keycaps nice and solid quality. These are soft and bubbly sounding in my opinion, not sharp and clicky. In prior experience with Razer, the price is a bit up there, but I would wager its worth it. Received on September 28th, 2025; will check back after a while to update review if needed.", "review_rating": ""}, {"reviewer_name": "Kevin T.", "review_title": "Shoddy Construction, Unresponsive key issues", "review_text": "Before I got this keyboard, I was using the 2016 edition razer blackwidow ultimate. That keyboard still works perfectly, and the only problem I had with it was that the keyboard was LOUD as heck.
Enter the blackwidow v4 x with yellow switches. At first i was extremely happy with the look, feel, and materials of the keyboard, it felt very premium, and the keys were MUCH quieter.
I bought it in December of 2023. By March 2024 I noticed an issue with the "P" key being unresponsive. Meaning when you press the key, there was a chance of it not registering the keypress. So if you press the key 10 times, it may only display about 5 or 6 times. Not that bad for gaming since the "P" key is hardly used. However when typing it could get very annoying. I attached a video showing me trying to press the button 3 times, followed by a space, then the button 3 times, then a space etc. You can clearly see it does not register the keypress quite often.", "review_rating": ""}, {"reviewer_name": "ben", "review_title": "great keyboard", "review_text": "absolutely love it great keyboard. really good for the price lighting on the rgb is amazing. so far it feels really durable.", "review_rating": ""}, {"reviewer_name": "mitesh", "review_title": "Best Keyboard", "review_text": "Fantastic keyboard as per my choice and also this works well. The package was all good at the time I recieved it. All items were there and the experience is amazing.", "review_rating": ""}, {"reviewer_name": "Steven", "review_title": "way better quality than expected", "review_text": "I've had my fair share of gaming keyboards but this one in particular feels great and was way better quality than expected.
It is relatively quiet for a gaming keyboard and has excellent tactile feedback.
The backlight is clean and vibrant as well.
My only complaint would be the macro buttons on the left of the keyboard, but only because I am personally not used to it from previous keyboards.", "review_rating": ""}, {"reviewer_name": "Lonely Sickoz", "review_title": "Muy buena calidad", "review_text": "Es el primer teclado que compro.
Es el estilo contemporáneo.
Estoy feliz con mi compa no se siente barata hasta la cuerda usb muy reciente.
Las luces son muy lindas.", "review_rating": ""}, {"reviewer_name": "Majid soaimel", "review_title": "Don't prefer Razer, but it's ZZZ so I made an exception", "review_text": "It's super clicky which I hate and it's not swappable which is absurd. The RGB is very inaccurate when setting up but when you do, it looks nice enough. I still prefer my KDA Logitech G Pro keyboard but I got this because it's miyabi <3 the keys are very nice to the touch, although I hate that the macro buttons are on the left, they're messing up with my muscle memory but I can get used to them. The keyboard is metal, cool to the touch, and heavy.", "review_rating": ""}, {"reviewer_name": "Rodrigo B.", "review_title": "Una edición muy bonita", "review_text": "Los switches son un poco ruidosos pero aún así me gustó mucho el diseño y la calidad del teclado.", "review_rating": ""}]

Title: RisoPhy Mechanical Gaming Keyboard, RGB 104 Keys Ultra-Slim LED Backlit USB Wired Keyboard with Blue Switch, Durable Abs Keycaps/Anti-Ghosting/Spill-Resistant Computer Keyboard for PC Mac Xbox Gamer
Description: 【Mechanical Keyboard: Responsive BLue Switches】RisoPhy PC keyboard features clicky keys which offer you higher accuracy and quicker response with an enjoyable click sound when typing.This keyboard is more comfortable to type on since it features deeper key travel,greater feedback,and more space between keys.For those who prefer keyboards with a more tactile and "clicky" feel,our keyboard with BLUE switches is a nice choice.
Category: Video Games,Legacy Systems,Xbox Systems,Xbox,Accessories
Reviews:
[{"reviewer_name": "jaycha2", "review_title": "★★★★★ Great first impressions!", "review_text": "Just received my RisoPhy RGB Mechanical Gaming Keyboard and I'm already impressed! Unboxing was smooth — everything was well packaged and arrived in perfect condition.
Right out of the gate, the mechanical switches feel fantastic — satisfying and responsive with great tactile feedback. Typing this review on it now and it already feels way better than my old membrane keyboard.
The RGB lighting looks amazing — all 104 keys are individually backlit with tons of color and lighting mode options. Instantly upgraded the look of my desk setup.
Build quality feels solid and premium — no flex, no creaking, and the keycaps have a nice, smooth texture. It's a standard full-size layout with number pad, so it was easy to jump right in with no learning curve.
Can't speak to long-term durability yet, but based on first impressions, this keyboard seems like an excellent value. Will update if anything changes, but so far I'm very happy", "review_rating": ""}, {"reviewer_name": "Gozer The Destroyer", "review_title": "Mechanical Gaming Keyboard – Over a Year of Flawless Performance!", "review_text": "After using this mechanical gaming keyboard for well over a year now, I can confidently say it's one of the best purchases I've ever made — not a single issue has come up the entire time. It's seen heavy daily use for both gaming and typing, and it's held up beautifully, including one memorable incident where I accidentally spilled soda right onto it; I was able to quickly disassemble it, clean it thoroughly with water and some rubbing alcohol, and it came back working like nothing ever happened, which speaks volumes about its build quality and durability. The RGB lighting is absolutely vibrant and stunning, with multiple settings and effects that let me customize the look to match my setup, whether I'm going for a subtle glow or a full-blown rainbow light show. The mechanical blue switches are honestly the sweet spot — they offer that satisfying, tactile clicky feel that's so satisfying for typing, while still being incredibly responsive and snappy for gaming, and thanks to the full anti-ghosting on the 104 keys, every single keypress registers perfectly even during the most intense, fast-paced gaming moments. With its rugged build, gorgeous RGB, fantastic switches, and full-sized layout, this keyboard has completely exceeded my expectations — I couldn't recommend it more to anyone looking for a reliable, high-performing mechanical keyboard!", "review_rating": ""}, {"reviewer_name": "Kat", "review_title": "Great for those with long nails.", "review_text": "I got this keyboard for a couple of reasons. I type at night, and when I wake up early, I'll do schoolwork. It's backlit and I can see the keys in the dark. There are a few settings to have the keys act or light up differently. And, because I have medium-long nails - the keys are large enough, and there is enough space between them, to accommodate my medium-length gel nails. I got raised keycaps to stick on the keys of this keyboard but they are not necessary for the length of my nails. Its appearance is as depicted, not too big, not too small. The keyboard connected easily to my laptop and is just as easy to set on top when not in use. It unplugs from the USB outlet easily, making removability a cinch when I decide enough is enough (not often) and pack everything up and put it away. It's very responsive, typing exactly as I type or game. None of the keys have stopped working or gotten stuck, even with my long nails. I love the sound of the keys clicking, again not too loud nor too soft. It gives me a 90s vibe while typing, and I can hear if I've hit the keys. Overall, I'm very glad I decided to buy this keyboard. It's perfect for my needs.", "review_rating": ""}, {"reviewer_name": "DC", "review_title": "Nice, blue switch. led mechanical keyboard that doesn't break the bank.", "review_text": "If you're looking for a slim, low profile, led mechanical keyboard with blue switches, then you will be happy with this. The keyboad is exactly as described in the listing. The keyboard housing is made of plastic which makes the keyboard lightweight. The keys have a nice tactile feel with a nice "clicky" sound. The build quality is good, but doesn't compare to the solid feel of my Motospeed or Red Dragon keyboards. Included with the keyboard is a little plastic keycap puller.
The led's are nice and bright and can be turned off. The CON is that each key is a set color, so if you're looking for a keyboard whose keys can change to various colors, you might want to skp this one. I personally did not care for any of the available 9 light modes. The 9 modes were definitely not exciting in my opinion and with keys being a preset color, I found some of the modes quite distracting. You can increase, decrease the brightness or turn off the leds. If you're looking for a keyboard where each key can display a multitude of different colors, this is keyboard is not for you.
As for the the sole purpose of using this as a mechanical keyboard, then you won't be disappointed. I purchased this for use at work because I love the tactile feedback of mechanical keyboards. I didn't not test the liquid resistance of the kayboard but there are cutouts on the bottom for liquid drainage. No key ghosting was detected during its use. Again, if LED keyboards is what you fancy, I don't think you will be pleased with this because the keys are a preset color and can't be changed. As for the function of being a mechnical keyboard, this works well for the price point.", "review_rating": ""}, {"reviewer_name": "zeroryouko", "review_title": "Great mechanical keyboard for productivity", "review_text": "Bought this keyboard for my office, as a replacement for a wireless, membrane based keyboard that was starting to show its age.
The value of this keyboard is excellent. Based on the feel, it seems to be a true mechanical keyboard with switches, and not a simulated one using a membrane contact with a clicky mechanism. The feel is great and the pressure is just right to prevent most accidental touches to adjacent keys from inserting extra letters. Nice and clicky, maybe not the best for noise if you're in an office with other people, but the feel is great and if you work in a private office like I do the noise won't matter much. I had thought the RGB colors would be distracting, especially for an office, but actually they are fairly subdued and actually seem to help with positioning (I am a fast hunt-and-peck 3 finger typist, so this actually matters a lot to me).
I have a much more expensive Razer mechanical gaming keyboard at home, and the main difference I see between them, other than cosmetic differences, is that the Razer keys seem like they have a hair trigger and require very little motion to produce keystrokes, while this keyboard is a bit stiffer and requires the keys to be depressed a little harder in order to produce a keystroke. So if you are relying on a hair trigger response for gaming, this maybe is not the best choice, although for a casual gamer like me it's more than adequate. Title: AULA S99 Gaming Keyboard, Wireless Green Creamy Computer Keyboards

Reviews:
[{"reviewer_name": "Megan Grape", "review_title": "Amazing Value for Many Features", "review_text": "Keyboard is amazing, has all of my needs met. It's a full keyboard with NUM pad, has a backlight that can be adjusted either by color, by pattern, or by brightness, AND connects to multiple devices simulataneously. The keyboard is *NOT* quiet. But it's a "thocky" sounding keyboard. The taps are thick, muffled, and soft. I do wish the booklet that came with it had better instructions. I couldn't find in it how to switch the backlight pattern and had to ask Alexa on the product listing after it arrived. But the booklet does show how to program the buttons, install the software, and switch between connection modes. I'm definitely a fan for the price. Other keyboards with these features can be up to $70+ so this is basically a steal and such a great product for the value.
I'd get more but because it connects to multiple devices, I only need one!", "review_rating": ""}, {"reviewer_name": "Amanda", "review_title": "Great!", "review_text": "Very nice key board! This is so nice. I've never had a really nice keyboard before and this thing feels very well made. The caps are soft to the touch and thocky! Though if you're looking for a quiet board for a dead silent office this probably isnt the one for you. However for a home office (or an architecture studio like me) this is not super loud and really nice even when I'm alone. The keys are very responsive and the dial is really cool! The rgb takes a second to work, i couldn't find the key shortcuts to change the lights but downloading the driver was easy and even though I haven't quite figured out how to get it to do what I want, I somehow managed to get it to rgb the way I wanted it to. So. Problem for later me! Would buy again, especially for the deal I got it for.", "review_rating": ""}, {"reviewer_name": "Jasmyn", "review_title": "Solid Choice", "review_text": "This keyboard is beautiful, it’s very easy to use, and sounds so creamy! Some of the videos including one I tried to make myself, make the sound appear a bit more “clicky” than it really is. The keys actually do have a very full bodied and creamy sound. It’s easy to type with for work or gaming really. The RGB lights are easy to navigate even if you don’t have the driver. And it’s build allows for easy typing and less tension in your hand. It has a pretty solid build, and for what you pay I’d say it’s more than worth the price!", "review_rating": ""}, {"reviewer_name": "Logan", "review_title": "🔥BEST KEYBOARD I BOUGHT🔥", "review_text": "This is one of the best keyboards I’ve bought on Amazon. It has a great build layout, the keys feel comfortable and responsive, and typing on it is smooth, quiet, and creamy. It was easy to set up and works perfectly right out of the box. It comes with a charger that is the new charger of many devices including Apple, = very compatible. The design is sleek and modern, and it offers excellent value for the price. I highly recommend this keyboard to anyone looking for a reliable, quality option.", "review_rating": ""}, {"reviewer_name": "Bradley", "review_title": "An excellent keyboard", "review_text": "I got this for my girlfriend, and she really likes it. She describes typing on it as feeling great, and she loves how cute it is. Not too sensitive to type on while not being too resistant to touch, not too loud, had no trouble using it with her computer. It was a good birthday gift.", "review_rating": ""}, {"reviewer_name": "Reasonable Consumer", "review_title": "Works. Just okay", "review_text": "This keyboard is adorable, has great soft (not super quiet, but soft feeling) key presses, its responsive, and it has great connectivity options. Its a happy medium between a full size keyboard versus a compact layout, and it's so easy and smooth to type on.
That said, the RGB backlighting does not work for me. I've followed the instructions sent with the keyboard, followed the troubleshooting instructions from AULA and from Amazon, used AULA's software for this keyboard, tried factory resetting, and googled for help videos or anything I could find. Reached out to AULA's support, and they were unwilling to assist and just directed me to Amazon. All I could find on Amazon was the seller's support information. At this point I'm just accepting that it's a defect and something must be wrong within the keyboard, and I'm not savvy enough to diagnose their hardware issues nor do I have the time or will to demand a refund or replacement.
The keyboard works great without RGB, but it was a big feature for me when purchasing this as it was mostly an aesthetic purchase. Yeah, I could have picked other options, but I chose this because of the price and I wish I hadn't. So, knocked two stars off for me.", "review_rating": ""}, {"reviewer_name": "._.Alex._.", "review_title": "Gaming and Office", "review_text": "This keyboard is pretty amazing. It's very easy to set up and use. I use it for both office-type work and online gaming. It is not a quiet keyboard, typing makes some sound, which I personally prefer.
I love the extra controls like the dial for volume. The LED lighting has a lot of customization, even including adding a custom color, if you install the " AULA S99 三模RGB版 " software, but there are also shortcut keys to just quickly flip through the preset modes/colors.
It has multiple options for connection(BT/GHz/USB), and they all work smoothly & without error that I've encountered. I like that there is the option to keep it on consistently if it's plugged in(USB), but I wish there was the option to do that while running on its charge too(BT/GHz). If it isn't plugged in, it will go to sleep with inactivity, but that's really my only complaint.
I have not noticed any type of lag or input errors when using it. If anything, it's a little extra sensitive and, when first using it, I was typing some double letters by accident, so it is very responsive. I found it to be perfect even for fast-paced online competitive gaming, which says a lot for a small and affordable company/product. For the price, it's a no-brainer.", "review_rating": ""}, {"reviewer_name": "Marcus", "review_title": "Cute, has a few quirks but good keyboard", "review_text": "I love this keyboard. Title: RK ROYAL KLUDGE S98 Wireless Mechanical Keyboard w/Smart Display & Knob
Description: Big Features on a Small Screen - Is there anything it can't display? Custom gif image, date. connection mode, WIN/MAC layout, battery status, etc.
Category: Video Games,PC,Accessories,Gaming Keyboards
Reviews:
[{"reviewer_name": "Heather", "review_title": "Excellent Keyboard With Minor Software Issues", "review_text": "This is my first mechanical keyboard, and I finally understand what all the hype is about.
The sound is incredibly satisfying. It has that nice mechanical sound without being overly loud or obnoxious, but it also isn't so quiet that you lose the satisfying typing experience. The typing feel is probably my favorite part—the keys feel incredibly smooth and satisfying, and so far everything has felt flawless.
The build quality is also really impressive for the price. It has some nice weight to it and doesn't feel cheap or flimsy at all.", "review_rating": ""}, {"reviewer_name": "Joseph Soriano", "review_title": "Great design. Great functionality. 100% Recommend if it fits your general specifications.", "review_text": "tl;dr: I am EXTREMELY happy with this keyboard. Build? Beautiful. Sound? Amazing. Functionality? PERFECT. Price? FANTASTIC. If this keyboard fits your specifications for your desk and you happen to work with two different computers at the same time, get it ASAP.
More details:
Previously I had a significantly smaller RK 68 which was great for me. It was perfect for what I wanted, a small profile and clacky keyboard. Unfortunately, I spilled soda all over it and it died so I had to get a new one. Fortunately, it was this keyboard.", "review_rating": ""}, {"reviewer_name": "Bearforce", "review_title": "All the mechanical keyboard I need", "review_text": "First mechanical keyboard I’ve owned, can’t imagine I’d need anything different. Bought two of these, one for my workspace and one for my wife. We both needed accurate and responsive keys for frequent data and password entry, the lights and display are just bonus points. I change out my display for random gifs and RGB weekly using the web portal, easy enough once you get the hang of it, takes 5-10 minutes to upload a gif. Can confirm battery lasts about a week with moderate workday use. Keys are on the quieter end of clacky, not as obnoxious as some mechanical keyboards I’ve used in the past. Key travel registers about 75% from fully depressed which took me a tiny bit of time to adapt to. More often now, I’ll think I missed a letter because I didn’t press quite hard enough, but look back to find it registered after all. Comes with a few replacement switches, key puller, and usb-c cable which is nice. I’m sure there is better quality for more money out there but I’m not the demographic for it, this is all the keyboard I think I’ll ever need.", "review_rating": ""}, {"reviewer_name": "L", "review_title": "My Favorite Keyboard That I Own", "review_text": "This is my favorite keyboard that I own - I do wish that the whole body were aluminum, but for the price this is a fantastic keyboard. I've switched out the keycaps and am currently lubing the keyswitches to give them a slightly less tactile feel and the keyboard is holding up well to my beginner fumblings :) I'm glad I went with this over some of the other beginner, more affordable mechanical keyboards I was considering as I feel like this one is a bit sturdier and offers a more premium experience for the price. I also love the colors, I haven't had any issues with the connectivity, the charge lasts a long time, and the RGB is bright and has a lot of fun modes. I enjoy typing on this one a lot - it's a deeper creamy I would say (maybe on the thocky side I guess) so if you're looking for a more linear feel or a higher pitch you may consider getting this and doing what I did and lubing the switches or changing them up entirely (there are a lot of really affordable creamy switches out there).", "review_rating": ""}, {"reviewer_name": "Emily", "review_title": "Solid quality keyboard at a fantastic price!", "review_text": "Recently I got bit by the creamy keyboard bug and i started my search for a keyboard that would give me that sweet sound that everyone seems to love.
After doing some research i came across this keyboard and decided to pull the plug on ordering it. When i received it in the mail the first thing i noticed was the weight. Previous keyboards i have purchased have all felt light and somewhat flimsy/thin. This keyboard is built solid! It has a great weight and quality feel to it as a whole. The keys are exceptional and have the perfect texture that my fingers really enjoy when typing.", "review_rating": ""}, {"reviewer_name": "Yaya Jones", "review_title": "Super creamy keys!!", "review_text": "My first mechanical keyboard and sounds exactly how I imagined! It’s nice solid , creamy click noise! So satisfying!!!
I loved the key color combo! The RGB lights are customizable, down to each key! Super cool. I am overall impressed with my purchase, as I was hesitant to buy something I wouldn’t like the sound of. I was also hesitant because there are so many options but I am glad I picked this! Good value for your money. The keyboard is heavy and feel super sturdy, doesn’t feel cheap. The keys were very responsive to touch and the Bluetooth was easy to setup with my windows laptop.
The only thing I don’t like is the look of the keys, they do have a sheen/texture to them I don’t like but honestly, overall, I don’t mind it at all!
Great buy!", "review_rating": ""}, {"reviewer_name": "Oggie", "review_title": "To many firmware glitches - basically unusable for any serious work", "review_text": "Today, I initially wrote a negative review of this keyboard due to issues with missed or repeated keystrokes, or keys continuing to fire until another key was pressed. However, after extensive investigation (because I really wanted to keep this keyboard for its mechanical build), I finally discovered that the issues were caused by an obscure, lingering USB driver from a device no longer connected to my PC. That driver was behind all the trouble. I hope this revised review is published before the original one, which is no longer valid.
After 15+ years of using Cherry MX Blue switches on a single keyboard that eventually got damaged, I was in search of a replacement. This keyboard seemed like a good option - more compact than my full-size board and featuring “tactile” pale green switches. I hoped they would resemble MX Blues in feel, just without the audible click. Unfortunately, these switches aren’t really that much (or at all) tactile. I don’t understand the claim. There is a point somewhere along the key travel where pressure slightly decreases, but you’d need to press very slowly and have an extremely sensitive touch to notice it. In actual typing, it feels - at least to me - indistinguishable from a regular linear switch. That said, I’ve gotten used to them and didn’t have much trouble adapting after so many years with MX Blues. And the 'thocky' sound still sounds nice.", "review_rating": ""}, {"reviewer_name": "Layten Thompson", "review_title": "A must have for anyone looking for an amazing sounding keyboard!", "review_text": "When I first got a gaming PC, I figured I didn't really need a super expensive keyboard and that a cheap one that sounded "clicky" and had lights was fine enough. I also didn't want to bother with charging a wireless keyboard. However, I started to hear from YouTube videos and TikToks about "creamy" and "thocky" keyboards. I immediately started to do research, because I was obsessed with the sound. This is one of those rare purchases that I cannot stop thinking about how happy it makes me. I have absolutely no qualms with it. Here's what I love:
The sound is excellent. Videos that I watched were a good indicator, but as other reviews have said, they really do not do the keyboard justice for how it actually sounds. The letters themselves are very creamy, while the function buttons (spacebar, shift, enter, backspace, etc.) have a much deeper "thocky" sound to them. If you're on the fence, at least try it and return if it's not for you.
The functionality is incredible. There are a ton of lighting options that you can play with. You can mess around with them in the software on your PC. But because this keyboard has a small LCD screen, you can also change them directly on the keyboard itself. I have mine set to light up the entire keyboard cyan from whichever key I press, expanding out.", "review_rating": ""}, {"reviewer_name": "Lorenzzzzo", "review_title": "Tastiera ottima, peccato mi sia arrivata palesemente usata", "review_text": "Premessa.
La tastiera mi è arrivata nuova ma palesemente usata.
La confezione era sigillata da un secondo adesivo applicato sul precedente, la tastiera aveva delle ditate, il libretto come in foto, il cavo di alimentazione addirittura pizzicato, tutti i sacchettini rovinati.
Insomma, se acquisto un prodotto nuovo quello dev'essere nuovo, altrimenti avrei preso un usato garantito spendendo meno.", "review_rating": ""}, {"reviewer_name": "RizM", "review_title": "Great mechanical keyboard and seller delivery support", "review_text": "The keyboard works flawlessly and has a really great mechanical feel and sound. The keyboard delivery was very prompt and thank you to the team for providing a hassle free online purchasing equipment", "review_rating": ""}, {"reviewer_name": "D S", "review_title": "Comfortable and Stylish", "review_text": "This is a great and reasonably priced keyboard. The key sound/feel is super pleasing, and the quick switch between devices/volume/effects with the dial and screen is awesome.", "review_rating": ""}, {"reviewer_name": "softchef", "review_title": "Good keyboard, with nice click sounds and fun to type!", "review_text": "Good keyboard, with nice click sounds and fun to type! The build is sturdy and the keyboard is heavy. I am expecting it to last long. I liked the small screen for configuration. There is a time display on the keyboard, which I don't find useful.
Once charge last about two weeks with bluetooth connectivity.", "review_rating": ""}, {"reviewer_name": "Amazon Customer", "review_title": "The sound and typing experience is amazing.", "review_text": "This is my 2nd Royal Kludge keyboard and I am very impressed. I've had mechanical keyboards from Logitech, Keychron, Corsair, Drevo and Redragon and I like my RK ones more. This one in particular is just super satisfying to type on. I love the creamy sound from the keys, it's unlike anything else I've owned so far. The green and clay-red color scheme also looks awesome. Keycaps are soft touch but not shine-through which is a bit of a disappointment but not a deal breaker. The little screen and knob is easy to use and actually useful. It's nice to change settings in a menu vs using function keys, and being able to check the time when enjoying full screen entertainment is also handy to me. My audio setup is also able to use the knob as a volume control which is an added bonus. All three connectivity modes work well for me - Bluetooth is reliable, 2.4Ghz is fast and reliable, and wired mode is also fast and reliable. Range on BT/2.4Ghz is average, but since this isnt really an HTPC keyboard I don't think it matters much.
My only complaint is the battery life. RK claims they have a gigantic battery in this keyboard but I only get 2-3 days of use between charges, and it takes a loooooong time to charge so it ends up being plugged in a little more than I'd like. If I keep the RGB lighting on the 2nd lowest setting, I can get another day or two of usage but I wish I didn't have to charge this keyboard once a week.", "review_rating": ""}]

Title: Cherry KC 200 MX Wired Mechanical Office Keyboard MX2A Brown Switches
Description: Wired, mechanical office keyboard with anodized metal plate: Equipped with our improved CHERRY MX2A switches available in 2 different variants - for an unmatched typing experience
Category: Electronics,Computers & Accessories,Computer Accessories & Peripherals,Keyboards, Mice & Accessories,Keyboards
Reviews:
[{"reviewer_name": "Paolo Traegini", "review_title": "Great keyboard and value, looks sharp too", "review_text": "OK, I have had a LOT of mechanical keyboards over the years, at various price points. Between me and my wife, we've gone through at least 10 keyboards each over the last 15 to 20 years (yeah, multiple PCs, locations, use cases, unhappy with some of them, etc.). Plus, I am both a software and hardware engineer (recently retired), so I have a pretty solid context for my opinion.
This Cherry KC 200 MX (with the MX2A Brown switches) is really very nice. Solid construction, a rigid metal base, and the keys have an excellent feel.
I got this one for my wife to use, replacing an extremely well-used Cooler Master Storm QuickFire TK Brown mechanical keyboard that came with OG Cherry Brown switches. She is a research professional that is WFH, and also does extensive creative writing and correspondence. She is also has petite, with small hands.
Well! She LOVES this keyboard - the keys feel perfect, their slightly closer pitch means this fits a full set of keys in a compact keyboard space. The keys are quiet but have a nice click feel. It has no RGB, which she never had a use for. The bronze finish is subtle and classy. And it fits in her space perfectly.", "review_rating": ""}, {"reviewer_name": "Firestarter", "review_title": "cherry kc 200 mx is my GOAT keyboard", "review_text": "My favorite key board.
I like the mechnical keyboard experience better than non-mechanical.
About five years ago I bought a durgod k320 87 key mechanical keyboard and love it.
Recently I wanted to replace a membrane keyboard with a full sized mechanical keyboard and tried the cherry kc 200 mx. It's better than the durgod with more stable keys, very little vibration, quieter sound and it has a great retro high tech look. I think mine was reasonably priced at $69.
Using the keyboard is a pleasure.
If you like the mechanical keyboard experience, I recommend this one.", "review_rating": ""}, {"reviewer_name": "Ben G", "review_title": "Awesome keyboard, highly recommmended!", "review_text": "I got this keyboard with the MX2A Brown switches and absolutely love it! I came from my 12 year old Das Keyboard with Cherry MX Blue switches after its left Ctrl key quit working. Over the years I had grown tired of the harsh click of the Blue switches, but of course I still wanted the mechanical feel. The MX2A Brown switches are perfect! They provide a very satisfying typing feel and the typing noise is now at much nicer level. They have a nice "thock" feel to them rather than a sharp click. They feel buttery smooth and I'm pretty sure I gained a few wpm with this board. It also has a nice heft to it; feels very quality-built.", "review_rating": ""}, {"reviewer_name": "Miguel Galvez", "review_title": "Generally, OK. Solid Aesthetic. But Lacks Customizability (No Hotswaps, No Key Reprogramming)", "review_text": "The keyboard is beautiful. The bronze-colored aluminum plate is a stunning, especially when paired with brown keycaps. But it wasn't for me.
For the key press, the "bump" was minimal and not as tactile as I would have liked it. Also the "bump" is felt mid-press rather than from the top. Compared to other switches like Gateron EF grayish, where the "bump" is felt from the top.", "review_rating": ""}, {"reviewer_name": "Sean Patterson", "review_title": "Great keyboard", "review_text": "Great feeling silent brown switches, nice quality build, can’t complain. Finally a suitable replacement for my old Corsair Vengeance K65. Everyone seems to make their own mechanical switches these days but the original Cherry switches are still where it’s at.", "review_rating": ""}, {"reviewer_name": "clotilde rollins", "review_title": "Loved it, but it has a huge build quality issue.", "review_text": "I was so excited to get this affordable and what i thought was a well built keyboard, but turns out it loves breaking keycaps. I had 4 keycaps break (and then I contacted cherry to get replacements for 3 of them) over the span of 3 months before I got fed up and refunded it once the fourth broke. It is a shame, because everything else was top tier and amazing, great switches, no flex and awesome feel. Just so disappointing that the keycaps kept breaking. (they would break where they connect to the switch the plus shaped thing.)", "review_rating": ""}, {"reviewer_name": "Ardy", "review_title": "Damaged in shipping. Still works great!", "review_text": "My initial review was upset that my birthday present had gotten soaking wet. After letting it dry and using it for the past two months, I can safely say I love this keyboard.
For such a long time, I've been a membrane keyboard user. I did try one time to switch to mechanical, but the keyboard I got was such an utter failure that I swore off mechanical keyboards for another decade. Well, now here I am trying another one after refining my choices and picking my features I want and don't want. This keyboard is perfect for my desires! It doesn't stand out, but it looks handsome on my desk. It has the exact amount of keys I use and nothing more. It's clean, it's simple, it's functional and feels really good to type on. I use it actively for both gaming and writing.", "review_rating": ""}, {"reviewer_name": "nick judd", "review_title": "Awesome wired keyboard for office setting", "review_text": "Awesome keyboard for the money. Title: SteelSeries USB Apex 5 Hybrid Mechanical Gaming Keyboard – Per-Key RGB Illumination – Aircraft Grade Aluminum Alloy Frame – OLED Smart Display (Hybrid Blue Switch)

Category: Electronics,Computers & Accessories,Computer Accessories & Peripherals,Keyboards, Mice & Accessories,Keyboards
Reviews:
[{"reviewer_name": "Barbara Smoyer", "review_title": "Great Keyboard and Great Features!", "review_text": "This keyboard is probably the best one I've ever had. It is built so well. It is made mostly of some sort of aluminum. It does not bend at all and it just feels very nice. I have had a keyboard that was so cheap that it bent even when I was typing normally (I don't type very hard), so this was a nice change. The metal volume dial is very high quality, and yet again, just feels well-built. There is also a little button that controls 4 things. It will pause and play your music, skip to the next song, go to the previous song, and open up menus in the OLED display. The OLED screen is very nice. It could be a little brighter, and the larger pixels make it harder to display certain things. But, what makes up for that is that with the program you can install, you can download apps that will change what the screen says. My 2 favorites are Discord and System Monitor. They RGB lighting is really nice. Each light can be its own color and with the program, you can make your own lighting configurations. The keys sound very nice. They are clicky, but too clicky. They are also easy to press, but not so easy that I could see myself accidentally pressing one. It also comes with a wrist rest. It magnetically attaches and feels very smooth and high quality. Overall this keyboard just feels very premium and super high quality. I would recommend it to someone who wants a good keyboard with some very nice features from a good brand and does not mind spending the premium cost.", "review_rating": ""}, {"reviewer_name": "Ken", "review_title": "Outstanding, with a possible caveat", "review_text": "Five months into owning this keyboard and it's easily my favorite keyboard I've ever had. Reasonably heavy so it easily stays in place even banging out page after page of typing documents, but doesn't feel like a slab of lead. The entire assembly is well put together; the keyboard has a nice, satin texture across the body and the keys, which feels great under the fingers, though it does show some oils more easily so I recommend regular cleaning/wipedowns.
This keyboard uses an odd hybrid system between mechanical/membrane, some proprietary/trade secret Steelseries BS, though honestly, if this wasn't pointed out to me after the fact I probably wouldn't have caught on. This uses cherry stems and switches, and the keys are naturally a cherry profile, so finding aftermarket replacements/decorative keycaps is easy as well. The keys feel responsive and clicky, delightfully so, when gaming or typing for general purpose. But there's a catch; it's a hybrid, so not truly mechanical. It does feel very good, but I have concerns that the membrane will wear down in time as opposed to a true blue mechanical keyboard, which will stay responsive and snappy for a lesser eternity where membranes begin to show wear after a year of heavy use. Time will tell.", "review_rating": ""}, {"reviewer_name": "Camilo Salazar", "review_title": "SteelSeries Apex 5 – Almost a 5-Star Keyboard, but Not Quite (4.76 on My Scale)", "review_text": "The SteelSeries Apex 5 left a strong impression. ### What Makes It (Almost) 5 Stars – The Good:😃
- Excellent Media Controls: The volume wheel is fantastic: easy to reach, smooth to use, and includes a click-to-mute function. The menu button also works similarly to the playback controls found on many headsets with built-in microphones or hands-free kits. Super convenient.
- Onboard Controls – No Software Needed: You can manage brightness, RGB colors, effects, profiles, and more — all from the keyboard itself. No software required. Only macros can’t be directly viewed or edited in menu, which is a small detail worth noting.", "review_rating": ""}, {"reviewer_name": "Ibrahim Amir", "review_title": "Great entry mechanical keyboard with solid feel and comfort", "review_text": "I bought this for my 14-year-old, and it’s been a great keyboard for both gaming and schoolwork. The included wrist rest adds real comfort and doesn’t slide around. No issues with software or macros so far. It’s a well-rounded keyboard that feels more premium than its price suggests.", "review_rating": ""}, {"reviewer_name": "Raymond Ligenza", "review_title": "Awesome!", "review_text": "Excellent individual RGB keys. If you're into the old school keyboard sound.", "review_rating": ""}, {"reviewer_name": "James Kitelinger", "review_title": "Nice keyboard - Amazon Refurbished just sucks", "review_text": "I have only had this keyboard for a few days at the time of this review, but from what I can tell it is a solidly built keyboard with a nice feel and decently responsive keys.
I did have to knock off a star though as the keyboard I received was in poor condition with two of the keys having keypress detection issues. This however was NOT the fault of SteelSeries as I bought this one from Amazon Refurbished.

Reviews:
[{"reviewer_name": "Akshar", "review_title": "As per Description!!", "review_text": "I’ve been using the RK Royal Kludge R98 Pro for a little over a week, and I’m honestly impressed with how much value this keyboard delivers. Design & Layout (5/5)
I love the 96% layout. It saves desk space but still includes a full number pad, which I use constantly for work. The addition of the volume knob is a nice touch and works great for quick adjustments.
RGB & Customization (4.5/5)", "review_rating": ""}, {"reviewer_name": "Liliyanna", "review_title": "Amazing gaming keyboard", "review_text": "So, i dont usually write reviews, but i felt i had to for this keyboards. the creamy clicks are AMAZING (its my first time having it so im super impressed.) the tiny screen is actually pretty simple and easy to use, you can customize the backlight color and style, speed, etc. the knob works perfect. feels great. it came with extra keys, a usb-c to plug in if you prefer wired, and a key remover. everything feels amazing, very high quality. its obviously not 10 pounds, but carries some heft that feels super secure. its got little folded stands to prop your keyboard up if desired, which i think is super nice. i love the color variety (i got the brown, for reference.), it can be hard finding a nice keyboard that is still stylish and pretty. im extremely satisfied, especially with the price being only 70 usd for this nice of a keyboard. i still have yet to use it, but im pretty confident it will be nice. ill update if anything happens!", "review_rating": ""}, {"reviewer_name": "Eric", "review_title": "I am surprised how much I actually like this keyboard", "review_text": "I recently purchased this item a couple of weeks ago and so I think it was a good purchase. First of all, they keyboard is super smooth and because of the switches, you do hear some clicks but they're not that loud, just enough to be satisfying. The product feels well-crafted with quality in mind. The keyboard stands; are the perfect size, not freakish large so typing for long periods of time is comfortable. I also like how they send you the "end" key in the box so if you don't like the volume knob, you can put the "end" key back in. I type 80 words a minute, especially when I am writing programs, I pleased on how well the keys on this board respond and the entire feeling of when a key is pressed. When I type superfast on things that are super important, I don't want my keyboard to fail me.
Now, there are a few things I don't really like about it but overall, like I said, this is a great keyboard.
- The volume knob: Hey, it works but personally, I feel that it is too close to the "pgdn" key so you really can't grip it like a knob. I kind of wished it had groves or something on the dial making it easier to turn. Right now, I just got to try and turn it little by little by spinning the know from the top down to the "-" key. That's about all the room you got.", "review_rating": ""}, {"reviewer_name": "walkebe", "review_title": "Absolutely Impressed!", "review_text": "I upgraded my home gaming setup with this keyboard after considerable research, and it’s been a joy to use for both gaming and typing.
Strengths:
Premium typing experience: The pre-lubed cream linear switches and gasket mount deliver a “thocky” feel and satisfyingly smooth keystrokes. Typing and gaming are both quiet and comfortable, with five layers of foam dampening any hollow sounds.
Customization: The included software lets me remap keys, create macros, and adjust more than 20 dynamic RGB lighting modes quickly. I loved being able to easily tweak the look and functionality.
Build quality: PBT double-shot keycaps with an MDA profile feel sturdy and resist wear; they’re grippy and comfortable for long sessions. The detachable aluminum volume knob is a treat for instant control.
Layout: The 98-key layout keeps the numpad and arrow keys but eliminates wasted space—a space-saving solution perfect for both gaming and work.", "review_rating": ""}, {"reviewer_name": "Alexander Campos", "review_title": "Solid keyboard for the price", "review_text": "So I upgraded my desk setup to include this keyboard. I did minimal research but I knew I liked the color and the number pad.
After having it for several months:
1. The keyboard is indeed "creamy" and smooth
2. The lighting is fun and the quality of the board is very nice.
3. It has a good weight and the volume knob is very helpful.
4. I am glad I didn't go smaller
5. The key swap capability is nice but I don't use it a whole lot.
Overall a good keyboard to replace my Bluetooth work one. I definitely think this a worthy upgrade if you're in need of one.", "review_rating": ""}, {"reviewer_name": "John P.", "review_title": "Amazing keyboard - so far", "review_text": "I was looking for a keyboard that had a nice compact profile, looked nice, has a volume control knob, AND sounds great when typing.
THIS keyboard literally hits everything I was looking for.
It's just the right size and weight - it looks and feels premium.
The keys have that creamy/clacky sound I was looking for.
The colors of the keys are great - but that being said - the backlights don't seem as bright as other keyboards I've owned, but that's not really a big deal to me - but it might be to some people.
Overall - I love this keyboard - now I just hope it lasts. I've read some reviews that make it seem like it might not, but I'm hoping it's durable.
As of this review, I've only had it for about an hour, so I'll update this review if anything changes with time.", "review_rating": ""}, {"reviewer_name": "Blizz", "review_title": "Buttery. Title: Razer Huntsman V3 HE Magnetic Mini 65% 8KHz Wired Gaming Keyboard
Description: PRECISION FOR COMPETITIVE GAMING – Dominate FPS games and esports tournaments with Razer Hall Effect Magnetic Switches featuring Rapid Trigger and adjustable 0.1-4.0 mm actuation for faster reactions, cleaner movement inputs, and personalized control
Category: Video Games,PC,Accessories,Gaming Keyboards
Reviews:
[{"reviewer_name": "Pablo Ladino", "review_title": "A huge upgrade from my BlackWidow V3", "review_text": "I honestly didn’t expect to like this keyboard this much. I upgraded from a Razer BlackWidow V3, and the difference is immediately noticeable.
The magnetic switches feel incredibly smooth and responsive, and being able to adjust the actuation point and use Rapid Trigger is a game changer for competitive gaming. Movement feels much more precise, especially in Fortnite. The keyboard also feels extremely well built and premium.
What I really like is that it isn’t only great for gaming. For everyday use, studying, and programming, I can switch to a normal profile and it feels just as good to type on.
I was a little skeptical at first because I was already happy with my BlackWidow V3, but after using this one, I don’t think I could go back to a traditional mechanical keyboard.
If you’re coming from a regular mechanical keyboard, this is a serious upgrade. Absolutely love it so far. 🔥", "review_rating": ""}, {"reviewer_name": "HikerBrian", "review_title": "Incredible for coding, even better for gaming,", "review_text": "This one gets reviewed from two angles. As a professional software engineer I live by the quality of my keyboard and have been opinionated about keyboards for more than 20 years, so I ran this as my daily driver for a week to test it out. It was quiet, consistent, and responsive. Despite the gaming branding, this is probably the best tenkeyless keyboard I've ever typed on. Turn the lighting off and it can be dropped onto any office desk without getting a second glance. The high quality PBT keycaps have a texture that doesn't go slick and greasy, and they shouldn't shine up the way ABS does after a few months of heavy use. The switches are factory lubed with a dense foam layer underneath, so there's no hollow plastic rattle and no metallic ping. It's also not the clicking like you get from mechanical switches. It's a low, dull sound that doesn't get annoying in a quiet room or on a call. The adjustable actuation mattered more than I expected for office use. Setting it deeper than a gamer would means you stop firing off accidental characters when your fingers graze the home row, which is something that makes most fast-actuation boards frustrating for long-form writing and code. The aluminum top gives it a solid build, so it doesn't flex or walk across the desk, and the detachable USB-C cable means a longer lifespan.", "review_rating": ""}, {"reviewer_name": "NhutDuong", "review_title": "Good", "review_text": "Good", "review_rating": ""}, {"reviewer_name": "AmazonReviewer", "review_title": "Love the design and layout, and the HE switches feels great! I also love the keycaps texture!", "review_text": "I have multiple razer keyboards from down to the 2010 black widow which is still going strong, and a few newer ones from last year and I love them, but when I saw this new huntsman V3 HE 65% keyboard I wanted to see how it was.
Build quality is very solid, it has a nice looking aluminum plate which is very sturdy and does not bend when I push hard on it, and it has a decent amount of weight to it which is not too light or too heavy. I also like that it has dual stage feet which most 65% keyboards do without with them, and I like the way they made the USB port going in the case so the cable can sit flush in it, which does help prevent wearing out the USB Type C port or getting broken.
And it feels really good while gaming or typing on it with the new HE magnetic switches, they are really smooth and has a nice clacky sound profile and it is very responsive, the PBT keycaps feels really good and I really do love the grippy texture they have on them that my fingers do not slide off them when gaming for long sessions, and they are shine through legends and they are very easy to see in the dark.", "review_rating": ""}, {"reviewer_name": "MK", "review_title": "Razer’s Hall Effect Switches Are a Major Improvement", "review_text": "Razer has made adjustable-actuation keyboards before, but its previous analog Huntsman models relied on optical switches. This is its first real move into the Hall effect keyboard space, and the switch change is not just a spec-sheet distinction. These new magnetic switches feel noticeably smoother and less scratchy than the optical analog switches I have used in the past, especially when pressing a key slowly or typing for longer periods.
They also retain a full 4.0mm range of travel, which is less common than I expected among Hall effect gaming keyboards. I can set a very shallow actuation point for movement keys in competitive games without making the entire board feel like a hair trigger. For typing, I prefer a deeper actuation and the full key travel because it feels more natural and gives me fewer accidental inputs. That flexibility makes the Huntsman V3 HE easier to live with as an everyday keyboard rather than something designed exclusively for ranked matches.
Rapid trigger works as expected, resetting each key based on movement rather than waiting for it to return to a fixed reset point. In shooters, directional inputs feel crisp and immediate, particularly when rapidly stopping, strafing, or changing direction. Snap Tap can prioritize the newest input between two movement keys, while Snap Flex adds another way to activate commands based on releasing a key. These features will matter most to serious FPS players, but the adjustable actuation is useful even outside competitive gaming.", "review_rating": ""}, {"reviewer_name": "Adam Darling", "review_title": "Elite Magnetic TKL Keyboard With Precision Control", "review_text": "The Razer Huntsman V3 HE Magnetic Tenkeyless is engineered as a competitive‑grade keyboard built around Hall Effect Magnetic Switches, offering adjustable actuation from 0.1 mm to 4.0 mm and a 100‑million keystroke lifespan (). This switch architecture eliminates debounce delay entirely, enabling instantaneous actuation and reset behavior that mechanical switches simply cannot match. The magnetic sensing provides exceptionally consistent input recognition, and the keyboard’s internal calibration system compensates for magnetic interference to maintain stable performance over time. Combined with the TKL layout, which frees up desk space for low‑sensitivity mouse movement, the Huntsman V3 HE is clearly designed for players who rely on precision micro‑adjustments and rapid directional changes.
One of the most defining features is Rapid Trigger, which allows keys to reset the moment they begin to rise rather than waiting for a fixed reset point. This dramatically increases responsiveness in FPS titles, enabling faster counter‑strafes, smoother movement corrections, and more reliable repeated inputs. Esports.gg’s testing highlights how Rapid Trigger transforms WASD control, making movement feel “snappy, predictable, and extremely responsive” — a sentiment that aligns with real‑world gameplay impressions. The keyboard also supports Dynamic Keystroke, allowing up to four actions on a single key at different actuation depths, and Snap Flex, which assigns one action on press and another on release. These features give competitive players granular control over movement, utility activation, and complex keybind setups, especially in games like Valorant, CS2, and Apex Legends ().", "review_rating": ""}, {"reviewer_name": "Amazon Customer", "review_title": "Hall Effect Makes The Difference", "review_text": "Huntsman V3 HE Magnetic TKL 8KHz Wired Gaming Keyboard | Hall Effect Magnetic Switches, 8000 Hz Polling, Razer Snap Flex,Razer Snap Tap, Rapid Trigger, Adjustable Actuation
So this listing is for the v3 ten key less Hunstman v3 8K HE keyboard specifically designed for gaming with hall effect switches and snap tap actions. The keyboard has an 8000 Hz polling rate and has onboard memory to store profiles.
I have both the v1 and v2 version of this exact keyboard so comparing all three of these keyboards, they all have the exact same solid build quality and sound quality which is a quite thocky experience. The keyboards are solidly built and made of premium material which leads to a very comfortable typing experience. The keyboard is constructed of a solid plastic and metal material which makes them feel premium. The keyboard is about 14" x 5" x 2" high and weighs in with a heft and weight that allows it to sit solidly on your desk.
I have been using this keyboard exclusively for nearly two weeks now and it is now my daily driver. I am thoroughly impressed by the HE switches and how very comfortable it is to type on. The software is the one short area as the Synapse software really does not effectively work on Mac but it does sort of work on Windows but don't expect much. The keyboard itself is highly customizable and allows for full customization in color along with key press. Also there is no Linux support either but you can use SignalRGB to control lighting. Also Synapse itself really bogs down your PC and slowly causes a memory leak which means you need to regularly reboot your PC.", "review_rating": ""}, {"reviewer_name": "Terrorgod", "review_title": "Maybe im ready to give Razer another chance", "review_text": "The Razer Huntsman V3 HE Magnetic Mini keyboard is the latest addition to their Hall Effect Magnetic keyboard lineup. If you haven't been keeping up with keyboard technologies, compared to traditional keyboard switches made by companies like Cherry, they are now utilizing magnets and lasers to create a much more responsive key press reducing latency and allowing for customizable key actuation based on the users preference. I am a hobbyist with keyboard tech, where I have built a good variety of keyboards with DIY kits, customized some of my own, and tend to go out of my way to try new technologies. This is my third time trying a Hall Effect keyboard, with my first being the Steelseries Apex Pro ( with HyperMagnetic switches) and the original Razer Huntsman.
I didn't hold onto either of those keyboards very long as at the time they were very expensive compared to their traditional counterparts. They also didn't wow me out of the box with their switch technology. Keypresses felt weak, as if there was no feedback to register that I had hit a key. It also took a lot of tweaking to get them to what I would consider a usable state with accurate typing. Which leaves me with the new Razer Huntsman, where I am happy to report it doesn't share any of these problems.", "review_rating": ""}]

Scissors
Logitech MX Mechanical
Logitech K650

[{"reviewer_name": "IKKK", "review_title": "Makes work a joy!", "review_text": "I never thought a keyboard could completely change how I feel about my workday, but this mechanical board is a game-changer. It looks sleek on my desk, types like a dream, and honestly makes me excited to type.
Specter Linear Switches: The typing feel is butter-smooth and remarkably satisfying. It has a rich, quiet "thock" without being loud enough to disturb anyone on a Zoom call or in the house.

Aesthetic: The white gives off a clean, premium, retro-modern vibe that elevates my desk setup.", "review_rating": ""}, {"reviewer_name": "Jay", "review_title": "Luxe and Life Changing ♥️", "review_text": "This is my first ever mechanical keyboard, and I have to say, it's really life changing. I watched sooo many reviews for so many keyboards and almost passed on this one multiple times. [ T H E F E E L ]

I don't even have to use a wrist rest. I'm also thankful for the full numpad, which was the deciding factor (alongside the cute, pink color!) between this and other low-pro keyboards. The gold-tone, metal volume button is also feels smooth and satisfying to use.
[ C O N N E C T I V I T Y ]
The keyboard connected to my Macbook Air immediately without a problem. Changing between Mac and Win layouts has worked flawlessly. The hitch was that I couldn't use the keyboard software or web portal to change keybinds. One thing in particular that I look for is how it feels when I type. I have long nails and my long nail girlies know, if the keys are too stiff, not the right height, etc, it can be very uncomfortable to type all day.
I have an office job that requires me to be on the computer all day and this is the one. The keys are low profile, but have enough give that it feels satisfying to type. The clicks are there both audibly and when you press on the keys (you can feel it), but it is not one of those loud clackers that you see online that will drive your co-workers nuts. It has some weight to it where as it does not feel cheap, but is not overtly heavy. It is compact, so it doesn't take a lot of room up on my desk which I love, and has a very sleek and modern look to it. It takes a minute to get used to the layout of the keys being all so close together, but now I have no issues. The only thing I have noticed is that the backspace key feels a bit different and more stiff than the rest of the keys, which are so reactive and that is the one thing that annoys me. You can choose to have the backlit light on or off. I appreciate that it does not have a ton of wacky colors, and instead is a soft white glow that is easy on the eyes and adds a nice look to an already sleek looking keyboard. I feel like the hunt for the perfect office keyboard is officially done!", "review_rating": ""}, {"reviewer_name": "Van Smith", "review_title": "Good keyboard with horrible wakeup latency", "review_text": "I bought the Lofree Flow Lite 100 Keys Low Profile Mechanical Keyboard after watching several YouTubers enthusiastically endorse it, but I've learned the hard way not to trust keyboard experts who love anime cat themed keyboards most of all and who never review keyboards objectively.
The Flow Lite is not a cheap keyboard regardless of people trying to gaslight you, especially considering its build quality.
It is a nice, compact, thin, illuminated keyboard which includes all keys that are most vital for work but are often dropped or relegated to fn+ status, namely home, end, page up/down, delete and print screen. The key legends are clean and the shine through illumination is even and crisp across nearly every key.
The very light typing experience is pleasant, but there are other keyboards in this price range or even cheaper that are as good or even better. The typing sound is good but nothing spectacular.", "review_rating": ""}, {"reviewer_name": "Amazon Customer", "review_title": "Premium quality", "review_text": "This keyboard is amazing. Il n'est pas très bruyant comparé à d'autres clavier mécaniques, mais il était encore trop bruyant pour mon usage, alors j'ai remplacé les switchs par les Hades et maintenant il est extrêmement silencieux.
